long_biography.plain_text:
Technology entrepreneur Robert Herjavec saw the possibilities of computer networking while talking to Ethernet inventor Robert Metcalfe at a trade show. Sharing printers through a network seemed a compelling alternative to connecting each computer separately. When his employer declined to change direction, Herjavec established his own networking business.

As his companies grew, he favoured repeatable procedures over relying entirely on unusually talented individuals. He also paid close attention to customers' spending plans, recognising weakening demand before the financial crisis intensified. His approach to assessing young businesses put particular weight on existing sales: paying customers demonstrated demand more convincingly than an attractive idea alone.
